subject: Some GOP candidates are still making election fraud claims
posts:
While many Republican voters want to look ahead, key candidates continue recycling disproven 2020 election fraud claims.
Evidence: AP reviews, polls, candidate statements
#Aletheia #USPol #Elections

Candidates argue they are championing election integrity and giving voice to persistent voter doubts about past balloting systems.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, +0.2) — Democratic Advocacy

Repeating debunked fraud claims without evidence weaponizes distrust to motivate base turnout, despite voter desire to move forward.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.8, -0.85) — Divisive Extraction

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Recycling disproven election claims prioritizes short-term factional loyalty over democratic stability.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 12.0, Uncertainty z: 3)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Campaign Messaging: FAIL (-0.85, -0.9) — Amplifying disproven falsehoods.
- Voter Sentiment: PASS (0.6, 0.5) — Electorate seeks forward progress.
Years after 2020, certain Republican candidates continue leaning into election denialism even as their own base signals fatigue.

The Poison:
Institutional trust is traded for temporary electoral enthusiasm.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing partisan political strategy (WHO) with objective electoral integrity (WHAT).

Social Physics Analysis:
Actors run a Smart Selfish Maneuver, manufacturing grievances about election integrity to maintain political mobilization while projecting blame onto established systems.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. Destructive forces dominate constructive governance.

The Unavoidable Truth: Undermining faith in democratic processes for political leverage weakens the entire republic.

The Unavoidable Lie: Repeating baseless fraud claims is purely an exercise in civic transparency.
